message: `aria-hidden="true"` on the `<div>` above it may take `error` out of the accessibility tree
$reason: The reference's message line inside a wrapper written `aria-hidden="true"`: the error part carries its `alert`, bound by nothing, and the text stays on the screen, while Chromium 141 and 155 drop the region from their tree (`ariaHiddenSubtree`) and Firefox 136 and 158 build no accessible for it (measured on 2026-10-20). Nobody announces the error, and axe 4.13 reports nothing on the page. Point 7 read the part and its role on the element alone, and passed it. The hint beside it is no defect: a hint is read as the control's description, which both engines compute from a hidden element.
